dimensions.note: Across all six readings Rena is analyzed as effort and pleasure held together: concealed strain and comparison with specialists in two fields (B0199 H:P170-P183), a recovered first pleasure in jumping followed at once by a higher bar (H:P205-P231, P245), a reported thirty-minute rehearsal of one move beside 'I simply like moving' (B0248 505018301 P17-P32, P41-P50), an art interest she thinks unlike her (B0232 case 15) and a receiver's surprise at being celebrated (B0239 P11-P12). Each reading keeps rivals open (care or deflection, recovered pleasure or renewed competition). Not C: no conditional procedure for an unshown situation is derived. Not E: the pattern recurs, with rivals tested, in six independently gated readings.

Only B0199 H has an internal sequence (strain, low bar, choice, higher bar, reported recovery). The readings refuse any order across the occurrences; 'pre-debut' (B0248) and 'after the completed live' (B0251 200500) are local horizons, not a chronology. E rather than NOT_ASSESSED because the readings affirmatively establish that the occurrences are unordered.

Located markers are few: the message title and its manager address (B0232 case 15), and くすぐったい for being surprised (B0239 P11-P12). Elsewhere her Japanese is paraphrased, and every voice cue in every reading is unheard. Not D: too little located wording to support voice.

Ordinary activities with stated reasons recur: running, shoe shopping and choosing a cute design (B0199 F, H2-H3), a solo museum visit (B0232), drinks for the trio and reluctant skin care (B0248 505018301, 505018304), doughnuts and tea during practice (B0250 507020102), and a home-party plan and shopping invitation (B0251 508021701). Many are proposed rather than shown. Not C: no procedure for an unfamiliar ordinary situation. Not E: located across five readings.

Distinct, located conduct toward several counterparts: the manager (requests, protests at overprotection and touch, the requested back slap; B0199 H), Kyoko (reads her strictness as responsibility, prompts her concession; B0250 507020101 P39-P65), Honoka (teasing corrected and apologized for; B0248 505018303, B0251 508021704), Sui (athletic rivalry and rematch; B0250), Coney (the audience-discovery idea; B0251 507020702), and the written board voices (B0239 P20-P22). Not C: no recipient rule is derived and most relations sit inside single families. Not E: the counterparts get differentiated, located conduct.

Interior states are self-reports or brief parenthesized lines: the inward limit and 'can no longer picture failure' (B0199 H:P251-P252), the recalled first jump (H:P205-P216), the receiver's surprise (B0239 P11-P12), and her no-comment appraisal at the manager's pause (B0248 505018304). Not D: no sustained interior is analyzed.

Friction is local and usually repaired: protests at being carried and grasped (B0199 H:P92-P95, P157-P160), the contested 'courting' exchange (H:P274-P275), the hook joke corrected and apologized for (B0248 505018303), mediation of the practice-slot dispute (B0250 507020101), and the apology to Honoka (B0251 508021704). Not D: no conflict process is analyzed across occasions.

Located normative content: apologies after teasing (B0248 505018303; B0251 508021704), recognition of the staff labor behind idol work (B0251 508021701), and a warning against jumping into the game (B0250 507020102). None is deliberation through a dilemma. Not D: local acts only.

Teasing recurs and each reading tests it against its costs: the withdrawn pet joke and the water-sharing tease (B0199 E, H:P79), the framing and leggings jokes that draw peer objections (B0248 505018301; CL-B0248-047, -051), the planned teasing of the manager (CL-B0248-059), the proximity tease (B0250 CL-B0250-024), the Kyoko pun (507020102), the teasing apology (B0251 508021704), and Kyoko's board caution about teasing (B0239 P20-P22). Not C: no generative model. Not E: an analyzed recurring device across five readings. A reviewer may prefer E.

Six complete units: one Intimacy family including the 290-page episode, one Short message, one Birthday portfolio and four Event families in three readings. The main-story states the readings cite as context (B0085, B0122, B0123, B0159, B0161, B0167, B0186, B0191) are not curated on this subject, which is the decisive gap for a main-cast character. Not D: narrow for the subject.

Affirmative limits recur: overwork named by the shopkeeper and her own later account (B0199 H:P140-P146, P264), the complaint that she would dance forever (H:P266-P267), Honoka's and Kyoko's objections to body jokes (B0248 505018301, 505018303), the correction of the hook joke, Kyoko's caution about teasing (B0239 P20-P22), objections during the game (B0250 CL-B0250-024), and the apology to Honoka (B0251 508021704). Not C: they remain located occasions, not a model of when the limits apply. Not E: they recur across five readings.

Only relative markers: next week, pre-debut, a local summer reference (B0250), after the live (B0251 200500), Christmas (B0251 200510). No year, age or placement relative to Main is given by any reading.

scenario_readiness.note: Her Japanese is mostly paraphrased, with a message title, an address and くすぐったい as the located wording, and every voice cue is unheard. B0248 gives multi-speaker structure but little quoted wording. Generated lines would be fluent invention rather than source-supported voice. This bounds the evidence set, not Rena's speech.

The effort-and-pleasure pattern is located in unordered occurrences with mostly paraphrased speech and uncurated main-story states. Extending it to a new situation would require inventing chronology, voice and counterparts' answers.

scenario_readiness.note: Running, shopping, a museum visit, drinks, tea and party planning answer bounded canon questions about these occurrences. Most outings and purchases are proposed or reported, and the readings give no procedure for an unfamiliar ordinary situation.

Apologies after teasing and recognition of staff labor (B0248 505018303; B0251 508021701, 508021704) are the only normative content. They cannot support simulating ethical deliberation in another situation.

The readings affirmatively deny an established romance: D's 'near my type, for now enough', G's qualified date comparison and the contested 'courting an idol' exchange (B0199 H:P274-P275) keep both positions; B0239 and B0248 claim no reciprocal romance. Simulating one would invent a relationship the evidence withholds.

Idol work appears in breadth (making-of filming, recording nerves, joint practice, post-live planning), but every performance is reported or elided and appraisals are peers' accounts (B0248, B0250 507020102 P94-P104, B0251 200500). CONDITIONAL would need a procedure the readings do not supply.

No performance outcome is shown: the higher-bar attempt has no result (B0199 H5), the making-of footage is not supplied (B0248), the dance contest is elided with no winner (B0250), and the 2nd GEAR concert and the Christmas event are reported (B0251).
No reciprocal romance is established; her appraisals of the manager are qualified and the courting exchange is contested.
Her teasing and body jokes draw explicit objections and at least two apologies, and the manager's unannounced touch draws her protest; candid play is not standing consent for any party.

The recovery in B0199 is a local turning point: she asks for a higher bar at once and the coda reports a complaint about nonstop dancing; later readings state that her current competence does not cure earlier dual-success demands.
The earlier main-story and Sub readings the readings cite (B0085, B0122, B0123, B0159, B0161, B0167, B0186, B0191) are not curated on this subject, so her main-story states are not assessed.
No performed voice, music or runtime was reviewed by any reading, and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.

dimensions.note: Episode 401006487 gives a located conflict: Rena (荒木レナ) conceals strain while comparing herself with specialists in high jump and dance (P177-183), recovers a remembered pleasure in jumping after a low bar (P205-216), chooses both activities because she likes them (P226-231) and at once asks for a bar above her personal best (P245). The reading rejects both a no-change and a triumph-only reading. It is one portfolio and one relationship; no conditional rule extends it, so C is not supported.

Only episode 401006487 has an internal order; the seven short addresses are routes with no chronology, and the reading forbids harmonizing them (for example, the shoe-selection accounts in 401001210 and 401006487). Earlier states are not enrolled. Change within one episode only.

The reading paraphrases speech acts rather than quoting Rena's Japanese: a tentative question about closeness, teasing paired with admitted nervousness, explicit withdrawal of a joke, the qualified near-my-type, the not-a-child protest and requested support. Register, self-reference and address forms are not in evidence, and the 33 voice references were not heard.

Several ordinary activities are located: offering a towel and a partly used sports drink, wanting help to buy cute running shoes, a proposed morning run, an animal film she usually watched alone and a proposed meal, the pet fantasy, running on a day off and choosing shoes after one tears. A good spread within one portfolio; purchases, meals and routines remain proposed rather than shown.

The evidence is almost entirely Rena with the manager: requested closeness, criteria for being seen as herself, protests against being carried, treated as a child and touched without warning, and a requested slap on the back. The shopkeeper is occurrence-local, and Kyoko and Honoka appear only as her attribution. One relation does not support recipient conditioning.

Parenthesized inward lines are kept distinct from speech (P251-252: the limit she could not pass, no longer picturing failure), and her remembered first pleasure is her present narration. Local and brief.

Bounded disagreements: the request to be put down and that a shoulder would have sufficed (P92-95), the startled objection to the foot grasp and to being touched in public (P157-160), suspicion of the shopkeeper, the negotiated one higher attempt and the contested courting exchange (P274-275). No sustained interpersonal conflict.
No ethical deliberation by Rena is analyzed. The consent questions in the shop concern the manager's conduct; nothing is established about her ethical reasoning.

Teasing is located across several addresses: the playful refusal to let him go, the used-drink tease with admitted nervousness, the withdrawn pet joke, the qualified date comparison, the guess-who arrival and playful reprisal in the shop. A short repertoire, not a model of when she plays.

The family is complete: eight occurrences with exact scripts and hashes, all 277 Japanese and name records, every native object, sprite output and background reported as read or viewed, with 81 context rows compared. It is still one portfolio; earlier readings are not enrolled and no performed audio or runtime was reviewed.

Affirmative limits are located: dance is hard despite athletic training (401000135), concealed overwork inferred from two-week shoe wear and wounds (P140-161), a plateau in high jump and dance errors (P177), the immediate return of competitive ambition, and the coda's complaint that she will dance forever. The higher-bar result is not shown and must not be filled from the separate personal-best report.

The reading affirmatively establishes that no chronology, calendar or unlock level orders the occurrences, and no Main arc date is assigned to the unnamed earlier incident. Only within-episode order is fixed.

known_limits.statement: The eight sources are conditional occurrences with no chronology or unlock level; only episode 401006487 has an internal sequence, and cross-case comparisons are thematic.
The higher-bar attempt has no shown result, and the healed foot and improved performance are Rena's self-reports without examination or measurement.

The manager's unannounced foot grasp produced useful information but drew her objection; the reading does not treat the means as consensual, and her later requested slap on the back is a different kind of support.
No performed voice, singing, music, sound or continuous runtime was heard or watched, and the promised live is not performed in the source.
Her choice of both activities is a local turning point; the reading says it establishes no permanent cure for overwork, and the coda's complaint keeps the problem of limits open.

The earlier Rena readings (B0085, B0122, B0123, B0159, B0161, B0167, B0186, B0191) are not curated on this subject, so the reading's comparisons with them were not checked. Missing support is not evidence of absence.
